question: Do attempted work and first-cut angular spread provide useful independent controls for mutable stroke branching?
decision: pending: retain without inferred range, internalize, or defer operation
hypothesis: More attempts may saturate on short segments; angular spread may visibly change branch reach independently of drawing style.

baseline.kind: private implementation experiment, not corpus baseline

comparison: Static frame1; raw mean absolute RGB difference and changed-pixel fraction plus root visual inspection; fixed camera and style, no normalization of bounds.
constraints: One baseline plus four variants; failed variants count toward eight-attempt maximum
Source-faithful transition/RNG semantics, fixed candidate implementation across comparisons
No public default or continuous range inferred from isolated values
No whole-brotes recreation claim from one pool

decision_rules.attempts: Expose as explicit work budget regardless of artistic density interpretation; recommend no density label if extra attempts mostly skip short lines without useful visual change.
decision_rules.angle: Retain artistic control only if readable branch spread changes without loss of defining cut/revisit structure; otherwise internalize and record evidence.
decision_rules.operation: Advance only if retained pool supports a clear edit task without callbacks or source-specific switches.
